summary_responses.response: The National Park Service has issued a final rule, effective December 21, 2026, that allows bicycle use on approximately 37 miles of multi-use trails in Kentucky's Mammoth Cave National Park, up from about 19 miles today. The rule lists 12 trails the superintendent may designate for bicycles, including eight new trails yet to be built, and removes the White Oak Trail and the Maple Springs Connector Trail from the list. It also creates an exception to the general ban on horses on park roads by opening the 5.4-mile Houchin Ferry North/Ollie Road to horseback riding, which the agency says will give equestrians shorter loop rides and a new route to the river. The changes implement part of a comprehensive land and river trails plan begun in 2022 because earlier plans were outdated and deteriorating trails were harming park resources and visitor experience. That plan, which would add about 66 miles of land-based trails, went through an environmental assessment and public comment and received a Finding of No Significant Impact in December 2024.

key_fact_breakdown.key_fact: The National Park Service final rule for Mammoth Cave National Park is effective December 21, 2026, and allows bicycle use on approximately 37 miles of multi-use trails.
The rule allows visitors to ride horses on the 5.4-mile Houchin Ferry North/Ollie Road, expanding equestrian opportunities in the park.
Under the preferred alternative, the NPS will add approximately 66 miles of land-based trails to the park trail system, representing a 72 percent increase in trail mileage.

The rule adds eight new trails for bicycle use, including Brooks Knob Road Cemetery Trail, Brooks Knob Road Trail, Crystal Cave Road Trail, East Entrance Trail, Little Hope Cemetery Trail, Sugar Sink Connector Trail, Sugar Sink Trail, and West Entrance Trail.

In December 2024, the Regional Director for Interior Region 2, South Atlantic—Gulf, signed a Finding of No Significant Impact (FONSI) selecting the preferred alternative from the Environmental Assessment.
The final rule opens the 5.4-mile Houchin Ferry North/Ollie Road to horseback riding.
